objective: Prove, for a deterministic local dynamics written as its space-time law (allowed states: the trajectories): (1) the knots (K1-K3) that contain a cell's value after T steps and otherwise only cells of the initial row are exactly the sets S + {y} where S is a minimal decisive set of the T-step map F_T (some setting of S fixes F_T, and no smaller set fixes it in any way) with |S| >= 2; a decisive single cell gives a tie, not a knot; (2) a T-step map has no knot exactly when every decisive set contains a decisive single cell, as for AND and OR of literals; (3) for linear rules (polynomial p over GF(2)) the space-time law is a linear code whose knots are its minimal dual words; at lag T the future cell's only two-time knot is the support of p^T plus the cell, so at lags 2^k (Frobenius) it has |supp p| + 1 places for every k (rule 60: Ledrappier's Frobenius triangles), while intermediate rows give smaller knots at other lags. Check every finite claim by computation with controls.
status: Proved 2026-11-08: written as its space-time law, a process's knots joining a cell's future value to its past are exactly its minimal decisive sets of two or more cells (some setting fixes the future value, no smaller set decides it); a future value has no knot exactly when it is a single AND or OR of literals, so pairwise memory is exactly the terms and clauses; a linear rule has one two-time knot per lag, the support of p^T plus the cell, with |supp p| + 1 places at every power of two, and smaller knots through intermediate rows (2 + w(T) in rule 102's light cone, T <= 6); in Life a cell's next value is knotted only to sets of four neighbours, never to its own present.
title: Knots across time are minimal decisive sets
